why.text: Basaltic, low-pH soils on steep terraces and mild ripening temperatures, plus fortification and ageing, give high-acid, long-lived wines.

styles.text: Fortified wine, from extra-dry to sweet, made by canteiro or estufagem.

climate.text: Low temperature ranges through the growing cycle; ripening temperatures are normally mild.

soil.text: Mostly basaltic with low pH, giving high acidity; high organic matter; vines on hand-built terraces (poios).

altitude.text: Altitude and exposure of the plots create microclimates; the spec gives no figures.

tastes.text: Fortified wine with high, fresh acidity and dried-fruit and wood notes. Drier types are light and balanced; sweeter ones fuller, with caramel. Long finish, richer with age.

styles.name: Canteiro
styles.text: Aged in wood at least 2 years; sold 36 months after last fortification.

styles.name: Estufagem
styles.text: Heated in tanks up to 50 °C for at least 90 days.

styles.name: Garrafeira / Frasqueira
styles.text: Exceptional quality, wood-aged, from one harvest year; complex, structured and elegant.

styles.name: Colheita
styles.text: Good-quality single-harvest wine, with dried fruit, caramel and honey notes.

why.text: Mostly basalt soils with low pH give high acidity, and mild temperatures with small swings mean slow ripening on terraced slopes.

styles.text: Wines in three colours: whites, rosados and reds.

climate.text: Temperature swings are small through the growing cycle and ripening temperatures are mild, so ripening takes longer. Altitude and exposure create microclimates that strongly mark the wine.

soil.text: Mostly basalt with low pH, giving high acidity and freshness, most marked in whites and rosados. Added organic matter keeps soils high in it.

altitude.text: Altitude and sun exposure create microclimates; recent practice favours lower elevations with better sun exposure. No heights are given.

tastes.text: Whites: fresh, light to medium body, tropical fruit, floral notes, lasting minerality. Rosados: red fruit, jam, fresh, balanced acidity. Reds: red and candied fruit, spice, present but well-integrated tannins.
